title: Residency validation and fallback playbook
summary: Operational playbook describing how to validate region pin enforcement and graceful fallback behavior for private deployments. Focuses on automated test cases, monitoring signals, rollback triggers, and stakeholder communication templates.
scope: Applies to Private deployments (VPC and on-prem) and Dedicated clusters where region pinning (customer-specified residency constraints) is enabled. Does NOT cover Hosted API multi-tenant routing unless explicit residency controls applied.
prerequisites: 1) Control plane access to customer tenant and deployment metadata. 2) Region pin configuration manifest (pin sets) checked into routing-configs repo. 3) Test harness with synthetic requests and per-request metadata injection. 4) Monitoring dashboards and logging (audit logs) available for the deployment.
validation_tests:
- Pin enforcement smoke: Send 1000 synthetic requests tagged with customer-org and location header for pinned-region. Confirm 100% served from matching AZ/region pool and see 'pin_match=true' in audit log.
- Cross-region rejection: Send requests with a disallowed source region and assert either (a) rejection code 403 with explanation, or (b) deterministic fallback to approved region depending on customer policy.
- Mirrored-store consistency: For deployments that mirror data across regions for read-only use, run hash checks on 100 files/keys and confirm no drift > 0.1%.
- Latency & SLO regression: Baseline token-latency distribution captured pre-change. Run 30-minute load test at 2x typical qps; compare p50/p95/p99 and confirm <10% degradation for pinned requests.
- KV cache sanity: Verify KV cache warmup persists across failover and that sequence-id continuity is preserved for streaming sessions.
- Audit record integrity: Ensure every decision (route/pin/fallback) produces an audit entry with request_id, decision_reason, policy_id, timestamp.
monitoring_playbook:
- Essential metrics to watch: pin_match_rate (per-customer), pin_denied_rate, fallback_rate, regional_capacity_utilization, token_latency_by_region, error_rate_by_policy.
- Alerts (examples):
  * pin_match_rate < 99% for > 5 min -> Pager to oncall + escalate to deployments lead.
  * fallback_rate increase > 3x baseline in 10m -> Page SRE and product owner.
  * audit_log_write_errors -> Immediate page (loss of audit = compliance incident).
- Dashboards: Provide per-tenant drilldown with time-series for the metrics above and sampled request traces (with model version, kernel selection).
- Log queries: example BigQuery/ELK query strings included in linked_artifacts; use request_id to rehydrate full trace.
- Sampling: For high-volume tenants, sample 1% of requests for full KV/cache debug traces; sample 100% of pin failures.
fallback_and_rollback_triggers:
Fallback policy types: 'soft-fallback' (serve from closest legal region), 'hard-reject' (deny), 'degraded-mode' (strip PII and continue).
Rollback triggers (require immediate rollback to previous config):
- Incident class A: pin_denied_rate > 5% and customers report service degradation (SEV-level).
- Incident class B: audit_log_loss or corruption detected.
- Incident class C: data divergence in mirrored stores > tolerated threshold.
Rollback procedure: 1) Pause new config rollout in console. 2) Revert routing-configs commit via GitOps revert PR. 3) Trigger canary rollback (10% -> 100%) and monitor for 15 minutes. 4) Run validation_tests smoke (pin enforcement smoke & audit records) before declaring RC stable.
Communication: Short incident note template in communications_template below to inform customers and internal stakeholders during rollback.
communications_template:
Subject: [Action] Residency config rollback for <customer-org> - <short-reason>

Hi <customer-team>,

We detected an issue affecting region residency for your deployment and have rolled back the most recent routing change as a precaution. What we saw: <one-sentence summary>. Immediate impact: <what customers see - e.g., slight latency increase, rejected requests, etc.>.

What we did: Reverted routing-configs commit <commit-sha>, revalidated pin enforcement smoke tests, and are monitoring audit logs.
Next steps: SRE + private-deployments team will run full validation and follow up within 2 hours with ETA for re-deploy.
Contact: <oncall name> (pager) and <solutions engineer> (email).

Apologies for the disruption.

— Redwood Private Deployments
audit_and_compliance_notes:
- Store immutable audit entries for every routing decision for 365 days for regulated customers.
- Signed attestations: generate signed policy snapshots when a pin set is applied; store in tenant vault with timestamp and commit reference.
- Controls: KMS-wrapped logging export for customers requiring separate key ownership.
- Regular audits: schedule quarterly residency compliance checks for customers with strict residency SLAs, include hash snapshots of mirrored stores and configuration diffs.
operational_tips_and_gotchas:
- Time sync: Ensure all nodes have NTP within 100ms; mismatched clocks can make audit ordering ambiguous.
- Clock skew during failover can cause duplicate session tokens; ensure idempotency keys used in replay.
- Be explicit about what 'region' means (GCP region vs cloud provider AZ vs legal jurisdiction). Configure policy semantics accordingly.
- When in degraded-mode, strip PII server-side rather than relying on client-side redaction to avoid leakage.
- Testing with synthetic headers is necessary but also run a small number of real-traffic canaries with opt-in customers before wide deployment.

notes: This document is a working playbook intended for the private-deployments oncall and SRE partners. It intentionally mixes tactical runbook steps with higher-level policy guidance so engineers can act fast while preserving compliance evidence. Update after any postmortem that affects pin enforcement behavior.
